prompt: In physics, the [...] of an object is the form of energy that it possesses due to its motion.

source.excerpt: In physics, the kinetic energy of an object is the form of energy that it possesses due to its motion.

prompt: In relativistic mechanics, $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is a good approximation of kinetic energy only when v is much less than the [...].

source.excerpt: In relativistic mechanics, $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is a good approximation of kinetic energy only when v is much less than the speed of light.

prompt: The kinetic energy of an object is equal to the [...], or force in the direction of motion times its displacement, needed to accelerate the object from rest to its given speed.

source.excerpt: The kinetic energy of an object is equal to the work, or force in the direction of motion times its displacement, needed to accelerate the object from rest to its given speed.

prompt: The SI unit of energy is the [...], while the English unit of energy is the foot-pound.

source.excerpt: The SI unit of energy is the joule, while the English unit of energy is the foot-pound.

prompt: The kinetic energy of an object is related to its momentum by the equation: $E_\text{k} =$ [...]

source.excerpt: The kinetic energy of an object is related to its momentum by the equation: $E_\text{k} = \frac{p^2}{2m}$

prompt: In classical mechanics, the kinetic energy of a point object, or a non-rotating rigid body depends on the [...] of the body as well as its speed.

source.excerpt: In classical mechanics, the kinetic energy of a point object, or a non-rotating rigid body depends on the mass of the body as well as its speed.

prompt: The kinetic energy of such systems depends on the choice of reference frame: the reference frame that gives the minimum value of that energy is the [...] frame, i.e. the reference frame in which the total momentum of the system is zero.

source.excerpt: The kinetic energy of such systems depends on the choice of reference frame: the reference frame that gives the minimum value of that energy is the center of momentum frame, i.e. the reference frame in which the total momentum of the system is zero.
